title: Halcyon Finance - Inference Ops Sprint Review
next_steps: Avery to share updated committed capacity pricing and burst policy - due 2027-12-12
Markus to provide route-level request profile (p95/p99 latency per route) - due 2027-12-13
Devon to run KV-cache + batching benchmark and share logs - due 2027-12-16
Schedule pilot kickoff for Dedicated pool (target week of 2027-12-20)
action_items: Avery: Share pricing and burst policy (2027-12-12)
Devon: Run 1k qps latency + KV-cache benchmark (2027-12-16)
Markus: Export top-30 prompt distribution and route weights (2027-12-13)
Rachel: Confirm compliance scope & data residency needs (2027-12-14)
meeting_header: Date: 2027-12-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood), Devon Park (Redwood), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM); Rachel Kim, Markus Li, Priya Rao, Elias Bennett (Halcyon Finance)
summary: Quarterly ops sprint review focused on usage growth, cost spikes for peak routing, reliability incidents tied to KV cache misses, and next-step planning for a Dedicated pilot and committed capacity. Agreement to run targeted benchmarks and share detailed route profiles.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted economics & burst policy
transcript:
00:00 - Avery Cole: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. we'll aim 45-ish minutes then quick sync - is that okay?
00:12 - Rachel Kim: Yeah that's fine, thanks. we had a couple recent spikes over black monday last week so eager to get into the numbers.
00:25 - Devon Park: quick note from our side: lina is on holiday so i'm covering the csm bits today. i'll run through the KV-cache benchmark plan after we look at your graphs.
00:38 - Markus Li: Good, i'll share screen in a sec. first high level, usage up 3x month over month on the recommendations route, most other routes are steady.
00:52 - Elias Bennett: and the product folks saw higher retry rates during the 11am-1pm window, around the europe region.
01:10 - Rachel Kim: right, and cost was the thing — our bill jumped and the finance team pinged us. we want to understand whether that's due to longer context, higher token counts, or model selection.
01:28 - Avery Cole: Understood. quick context, most of the spike you describe maps to p95 latency timeouts that caused retries which look like a cascade. Devon, can you explain KV caching behavior that might lead to that?
01:45 - Devon Park: sure. so on Redwood hosted, we do prefix and KV cache. when cache hit rates drop, request latency increases because more tokens move through the full attention kernels. there was also a small bug in our autoscaler config that allowed some backpressure during burst windows — we patched that last week.
02:12 - Priya Rao: we did see a spike in miss rate for the recommendation model, which aligns with a higher cardinality of user prompts. is there a knob for cache key normalization?
02:30 - Devon Park: yes, you can normalize prefixes and we can suggest a mapping that reduces cardinality. we'll send a suggested pre-processing step.
02:45 - Rachel Kim: can you quantify impact — like if we normalize we expect x% fewer token ops?
02:54 - Avery Cole: from our initial sims, normalizing prefixes and enabling 32k VK quantization reduced per-token cost by approx 18-24% for similar throughput. caveat: those sims were on a smaller corpus so we'll need your real prompts to be precise.
03:18 - Markus Li: When you say quantization, do you mean lossy INT8 paths? we have strict quality bar for financial text so can't degrade hallucination rates.
03:30 - Devon Park: good question. Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles by workload — some models tolerate heavier quantization, others not. we'll include quality regression checks in the benchmark plan so you can validate.
03:48 - Elias Bennett: who owns the quality checks? do we run them or do redwood provide the eval harness?
03:55 - Lina Gomez (recorded earlier comment): we can provide the eval harness and run examples; for pilot we usually run joint evals with customer prompts.
04:08 - Rachel Kim: ok that's helpful. next, the economics — what are the committed capacity options and how does burst billing work? we need predictability.
04:22 - Avery Cole: we offer Dedicated reserved pods with monthly commits. burst capacity can be configured — you pay the difference if you exceed committed throughput. i'll share a pricing sheet after this call with examples aligned to your 3x growth scenario.
04:40 - Priya Rao: is there a hard throttle if we exceed burst? we can't have silent failures during market hours.
04:48 - Avery Cole: we recommend graceful degradation policies: route-based fallbacks to lower-cost model variants or regional fallback. hard throttles are optional; we can set alerting first.
05:05 - Rachel Kim: tell us about observability — we need per-route token breakdown, per-token latency, and token-level cost.
05:15 - Devon Park: the Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns, cost per model, and trace ids. we can enable longer retention for audit logs as an add-on; that will be in the pricing doc.
05:31 - Markus Li: can we get a CSV export of route-level data? our platform team wants to ingest into internal dashboards.
05:39 - Devon Park: yep, we can export JSON/CSV. i'll coordinate with you after the call to whittle down the exact fields.
06:00 - Elias Bennett: there was also a reliability incident note — a 15-minute degradation last month. can someone recap root cause?
06:10 - Avery Cole: yes, that was related to autoscaler config + a rare cache eviction pattern. the autoscaler didn't scale early enough for a sustained 700 qps burst on the recommendations model. we pushed a config change and a mitigation that pre-warms the kv cache for warm routes.
06:30 - Rachel Kim: did that fix persist? we still saw smaller tail latencies a couple days later.
06:36 - Devon Park: the fix reduced incidence by about 85% in our next window, but your traffic shape still spikes; pre-warming helps but isn't perfect for very high cardinality prompts. we'll run targeted bench to reproduce your exact distribution.
06:56 - Priya Rao: for the bench, what infra do you spin up? we want to be sure it's representative of production.
07:03 - Devon Park: we'll mirror your route mix and concurrency, run 1k qps sustained for 10 minutes and capture p50/p95/p99 and the cache hit rates. we'll also try different batching configurations to find the cost/latency pareto.
07:20 - Rachel Kim: sounds good. i'd like the bench to include a test against a Dedicated pod with reserved capacity vs hosted with autoscaling to compare unit economics.
07:31 - Avery Cole: totally — that's the exact pilot we suggest. pilot plan: 2-week dedicated pilot, representative traffic replay, joint evals, and a quick cutover test.
07:45 - Markus Li: how invasive is the pilot? do we need network changes for VPC/private?
07:50 - Avery Cole: no network changes for Dedicated in the hosted offering; it runs in our cloud. Private/VPC is a separate project. for Dedicated we just provision reserved pods and route traffic. for VPC you'd need firewall rules and peering.
08:05 - Rachel Kim: compliance question — we process EU financial data, need data residency and audit logs. what's required?
08:15 - Lina Gomez: we have a private deployment option; also we support region pinning to EU regions and extended audit retention. we'll surface SOC2 docs and a runbook.
08:28 - Priya Rao: do you support customer-managed KMS?
08:32 - Devon Park: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations. for hosted Dedicated we offer envelope encryption with provider-managed keys but can do custom if required under a support/contract amendment.
08:50 - Elias Bennett: okay great. now onto cost drivers — what did you see as the top three for our bill?
08:58 - Devon Park: top three: model size/variant selection (larger models cost more per token), long context windows (more tokens), and cache miss rates that increase per-token compute. also inefficient batching can create per-request overhead.
09:15 - Rachel Kim: is there a quick checklist we can apply to reduce spend without changing SLAs?
09:22 - Avery Cole: yes: 1) prefix normalization, 2) tune batching settings (max batch size vs latency tradeoff), 3) pin lower-cost model variants on non-critical routes, 4) use KV cache warmers for hot prefixes.
09:38 - Markus Li: for batching, what latencies do you typically see at p95 with batch size 8 vs 16 on our type of models?
09:45 - Devon Park: rough ballpark: batch8 p95 ~ 180-220ms, batch16 p95 ~260-320ms depending on model and input length. exact numbers vary; that's why we want to run the bench with your prompts.
10:00 - Rachel Kim: okay let's get those numbers.
10:05 - Devon Park: On the bench we'll capture token counts, batching efficiency, and percent of requests served from KV.
10:12 - Elias Bennett: quick interruption — are there any feature flags we should flip in the next sprint to reduce risk?
10:18 - Avery Cole: yes, enable route-level fallback and increase cache retention for your top-100 prefixes. we can also temporarily lower concurrency thresholds for experimental routes.
10:30 - Rachel Kim: i'd like to schedule a 30-minute pilot kickoff meeting, include finance for pricing approval.
10:36 - Avery Cole: noted. i'll send a Doodle but target week of Dec 20 as suggested.
10:44 - Markus Li: one more: we'll need an export of recent error traces for the week of 2027-11-29 to correlate with our internal logs.
10:53 - Devon Park: we can export traces and correlate using trace ids; i'll include instructions in the follow-up.
11:02 - Rachel Kim: what's the escalation path if we hit production latency again during market hours?
11:07 - Lina Gomez: we have a 24/7 oncall for enterprise customers with a runbook; for Dedicated customers we offer priority response SLAs under the enterprise tier.
11:18 - Priya Rao: please confirm the RTO/RPO for incidents under that SLA.
11:22 - Avery Cole: i'll include SLA cliff notes in the pack.
11:26 - Elias Bennett: any blockers from Redwood's side to run the pilot?
11:30 - Devon Park: none technical; we just need your route profile and a signed pilot MOU. legal can handle the MOU once we share the template.
11:40 - Rachel Kim: timeline wise — when can we expect the bench results after we hand over profiles?
11:44 - Devon Park: typically 4-5 business days for bench + quality regressions, assuming we get the prompt corpus the same day.
11:54 - Avery Cole: recap and next steps: i'll share the pricing + burst policy and SLA cliff notes by Dec 12; Markus will share route profiles by Dec 13; Devon will run the bench and deliver results by Dec 16; Rachel to confirm compliance scope by Dec 14; we'll target pilot kickoff week of Dec 20.
12:20 - Rachel Kim: sounds good, thanks everyone.
12:25 - Markus Li: thanks all.
12:30 - Avery Cole: thanks, we'll follow up with the notes and the docs. meeting adjourned.
__notes_for_indexing: QBR-style checkin focusing on usage spike, KV cache, batching, Dedicated pilot. Important artifacts: pricing sheet, bench plan, export of route-level CSV, pilot MOU. Medium transcription quality with minor mis-hearings and occasional generic speaker labels.
